questions.questionTextEn: Amendment in (One hundred third Article 15 Amendment) Act, 2019 63. Consider the following statements: 1. The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an Article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2. The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India as being violative of the independence of judiciary. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: (एक सौ तीसरा अनुच्छेद 15 संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 में संशोधन 63. निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. भारत के संविधान में 44वें संशोधन ने प्रधान मंत्री के चुनाव को न्यायिक समीक्षा से परे रखने वाला एक अनुच्छेद पेश किया। 2. भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने भारत के संविधान के 99वें संशोधन को न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता का उल्लंघन बताते हुए रद्द कर दिया। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). In 1975, Parliament passed the 39th amendment to the con- stitution which removed the authority of Supreme Court to adjudicate petitions regarding elections of the president, vice president, Prime Minister and Speaker of Lok Sabha. This amendment was nulliﬁ ed by 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. Hence Statement 1 is wrong. Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th amendment to the constitution (2014). This amendment created a body named NJAC- National judicial appointment committee. S.C. struck down NJAC as it impinges upon the principles of 'independence of judiciary" as well as "separation of powers". Oﬃ cial Language *Oﬃ cial language is mentioned in part-XVII (Art. 343-351) of the Indian constitution. *According to Art. 343, the oﬃ cial language of the union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script and the digits used for oﬃ cial purpose shall be international form of Indian numerals. *According to Article 344, the president has the power to form a commission related to oﬃ cial language. *First oﬃ cial language commission under the chairmanship of B.G. Kher was constituted in 1955. *According to Art. 344 (4) there is a provision to form a 30 member joint parliament committee on oﬃ cial language. The committee consists of 20 members from Lok Sabha and 10 members from Rajya Sabha. *Any language canbe added in Indian constitution under the 8th Schedule. *Initially only 14 languages were added to the Indian constitution. *'Sindhi' language was added to Indian constitution by 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967. *Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali were added by 71st constitutional Amendment Act 1992 in 8th schedule. *In 2003, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and santhali were added by 92nd Constitutional Amendment. At present total 22 languages are there in 8th schedule. The state can choose any one Language as the oﬃ cial language. *There is description of oﬃ cial language for communication between two states or between a state and the union in Article 346. *According to Article 347, there is a special provision relating to language spoken by a section of population of a state. *Hindi was declared as the oﬃ cial language on 14th September 1949. *14 September is celebrated as the Hindi Diwas. According to Article 348 (1) (a), all proceedings in the Supreme Court and every high court shall be done in English language. *According to Article 350 (a), there is a provision of facilities for instruction in mother tongue at primary stage. Article 350B provides for establishment of a special oﬃ cer for linguistic minorities. The oﬃ cer shall be appointed by president and shall investigate all matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities, reporting directly to president. 1. Which Article of the Constitution provides that every state shall endeavour to provide an adequate facility for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage of education? (a) Article 349 (b) Article 350 (c) Article 350-A (d) Article 351 U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2003 U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2002 U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002 I.A.S. (Pre) 2001 Ans. (c) According to Article 350-A it shall be the endeavour of every State and every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups; and the President may issue such directions to any State as he considers necessary or proper for securing the provision of such facilities (7th Amendment Act, 1956). 2. Which one of the following is correct about the languages mentioned in the Constitution of India? (a) State can compel the linguistic minorities to choose their mother tongue as a medium of instruction in primary schools. (b) ‘Angika’ is now included in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution. (c) Hindi is National language of India. (d) Bodo is a recognized language in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution. U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016 Ans. (d) Bodo is a recognized language mentioned in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Bodo was included by 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 while other options are not correctly related to the languages mentioned in the Constitution of India. According to Article 343, Hindi is the oﬃ cial language of the Union not the National Language of India. 3. Under Article 344 of Indian Constitution, the ﬁ rst ‘Oﬃ cial Language Commission’ was established- (a) In 1950 under the Chairmanship of K.M. Munshi (b) In 1955 Under the Chairmanship of B.G. Kher (c) In 1960 under the Chairmanship of M.C. Chagala (d) In 1965 under the Chairmanship of Humayun Kabir U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1998 Ans. (b) According to Article 344 of the Indian Constitution, Dr. Rajendra Prasad appointed the First Official Language Commission under the chairmanship of B. G. Kher on 7 June, 1955. The Commission submitted its report in 1956. It recommended a number of steps to replace English with Hindi eventually. The Parliamentary Committee on Oﬃ cial Language, chaired by Govind Ballabh Pant was constituted in 1957 to review the Kher Commissions report. 4. Which of the following languages was added in the eighth schedule of the Constitution in 2003? (a) Konkani (b) Sindhi (c) Manipuri (d) Santhali Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2005 Ans. (d) Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognizes 22 regional languages as the official language of the Union. Originally, there were only fourteen languages in this Schedule, the ﬁ fteenth language, Sindhi, was added by the 21st Constitution Amendment in 1967, and three languages, Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali, were added by the 71st Amendment in August 1992. *Four more languages Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003. *Thus there are total 22 languages included in the eighth schedule: 1. Assamese 2. Bengali 3. Bodo 4. Dogri 5. Gujarati 6. Hindi 7. Kannada 8. Kashmiri 9. Malayalam 10. Maithili 11. Marathi 12. Oriya 13. Panjabi 14. Sanskrit 15. Sindhi 16. Tamil 17. Telugu 18. Santali 19. Urdu 20. Konkani 21. Manipuri and 22. Nepali.

optionsEn: a simple majority of its members
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). There is a fundamental diﬀ erence between the Hindi and English versions of the above question. In the Hindi format the question has asked about the oﬃ cial language in context of Constitution of India whereas in the English format the question focuses on the Parliament's authority of amending the oﬃ cial language of India. Hence, the nuances so present, create a contradictory nature among the intellects to resort to a conclusion. *Part XVII of the constitution deals with the oﬃ cial language in Article 343 to 351. Its provisions are divided into four heads- a. Language of the Union b. Regional Languages c. Language of the Judiciary d. Texts of Laws and special directives Thus it is quite evident from above context that the term 'The Oﬃ cial Language of India' is nonewhere mentioned in the Indian constitution. If we ignore the above mentioned 'mistake' or 'ambiguity' for the quiz, then it seems that the question relates to "the oﬃ cial language of the Union". As mentioned in the ﬁ rst paragraph of this interpretation, due to the diﬀ erence between the Hindi and English forms of the question, the answer will also be diﬀ erent. According to Hindi form, option (b) is correct. Amendment to Article 343, 344, 346 and 348 (1) (b) is possible only by the Parliament according to the overwhelming process mentioned in Article 368 (2), otherwise not. The amendment in above mentioned Articles i.e. 343, 344, 346 & 348 (1) does not require ratiﬁ cation of the state legislatures. On the other hand, if the English form of the question is accepted, then option (a) will be the correct answer. According to article 343 (3) of constitution, Parliament is authorised for creating an exception to Article 343 (1). As per Article 100 (1), such a law will be made by Parliament with its simple majority. The Parliament has enacted the Oﬃ cial Language Act, 1963, using its power. According to Section 3 of this Act, in addition to Hindi, English will also be used as the oﬃ cial language of the Union, from January 26, 1965. For some of the Union Government's purposes, English is mandatory. Clearly, any amendment in the said act can be made by Parliament with its simple majority and accordingly, the oﬃ cial language of the Union can be amended according to the constitution. The word 'Provision' used in the English form of the question and the word 'Under the constitution' are being clariﬁ ed in the article 343 (3) of the constitution. Thus to elucidate there are two distinct answers to the same question.
